Interference Search isn’t meant to teach a model that 4 × 4 = 16. The arithmetic on the search side is exact. The problem is choosing and composing operations without exploring the same effective state repeatedly. With six numbers, 831,176 possible paths collapsed into 13,229 distinct states. That is where the saving comes from.
I do agree that saying “models reason in a line” is too broad. Models clearly compile common operations into their weights. Call that memoization if you want. The interesting version of Interference Search would let those reliable operations remain atomic, then externalize the parts that still require search, merge equivalent outcomes, and remove dead states.
The 128-digit multiplication is cool, but it doesn’t really argue against any of that. It shows that a model can execute a long arithmetic procedure. It doesn’t show that combinatorial search, repeated states, and losing valid solutions have disappeared.
